prerequisites.concept: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties

evidence.quote: asks for this conclusion when the original class is only known to be a rational Hodge class

outputs.exact_statement: For an abelian variety with good reduction, the realizations of an absolute Hodge class are compatible with the de Rham and crystalline comparison isomorphisms. In particular, the $p$-adic crystalline tensor obtained from its $p$-adic étale realization agrees, after extension of scalars, with the de Rham–crystalline realization in Theorem 1. These compatibilities respect tensor operations, duals, Tate twists, divisor classes, and rational homomorphisms.* *The same assertion applies to auxiliary abelian varieties with good reduction over a finite extension of $K_0$, using a complex embedding of an algebraic closure of their field of definition.
If $\alpha$ has the Lefschetz pairing property on $Y$ and $f\in\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}^0(X,Y)$, then $f^*\alpha$ has that property on $X$.

Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be abelian schemes over $R$, with special fibers $X_0,Y_0$, and let $f_0\in\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}^0(X_0,Y_0)$. If its contravariant crystalline map preserves the Hodge filtrations, then $f_0$ lifts uniquely to a rational homomorphism $\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$.*

*In particular, a symmetric rational homomorphism $X_0\to X_0^\vee$ with this property lifts to a rational divisor class on the generic fiber. Algebraic identities among finitely many such lifted maps remain valid.

Let $A/\overline{\mathbb Q}$ be an abelian variety of positive dimension with good reduction at $w$, and put $V=H_1(A(\mathbb C),\mathbb Q)$. Suppose $$G\subset\mathop{\mathrm{GSp}}(V,\psi)$$ is connected reductive, its Hodge homomorphism $h$ gives the Hodge structure of $A$, and its conjugacy class $X$ makes this inclusion a Hodge embedding. Let $\gamma$ be a rational Hodge class of codimension $r$, represented on $V$ by an alternating form satisfying [eq:transport-multiplier].* *Then there exist a positive integer $n$, an auxiliary good-reduction abelian variety $B$, a quasi-isogeny $a:A_0^n\to B_0$, and a rational Hodge class $\kappa$ of codimension $r$ on $B$ such that, for the first-factor inclusion $j:A_0\to A_0^n$, $$(aj)^*\kappa_0=\gamma_0. \label{eq:transport-class}$$ The equality holds simultaneously in every $\ell$-adic realization with $\ell\ne p$ and in the crystalline realization after extension to $C_w$. Either of the following two further specifications can be imposed.* 1. *The variety $B$ is of CM type and is defined over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, with its indicated good reduction at $w$.* 2. *Put $D_A=H^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\mathbb F))[1/p]$. Suppose $\mathcal F_A$ is a filtration in degrees $0,1$ on $D_A$, over a finite extension of $K_0$, which is weakly admissible and has finite local-field descent together with the specialized tensors specifying the $G$-structure. Suppose also that, after a geometric tensor-preserving identification, it lies in the $G$-orbit of the original Hodge filtration. Then $B$ can be defined over a finite extension $K/K_0$ inside $C_w$, and $a$ can be chosen so that $$a^*\mathop{\mathrm{Fil}}^1H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(B/K) =(\mathcal F_A^1)^{\oplus n}. \label{eq:transport-prescribed-filtration}$$ Here the equality is made after a common finite extension and crystalline–de Rham identification. To discuss Hodge classes on this $B$, choose a complex embedding of an algebraic closure of $K$ extending the fixed embedding of $\overline{\mathbb Q}$.* *In the second case the realizations of $\kappa$ are supplied by the canonical tensor sections of the Hodge-type model and the polarization. In the first case these agree with the usual realizations and specialization of its absolute Hodge class.

Let $$(G,X)\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow
 (\mathop{\mathrm{GSp}}(V,\psi),X_{\mathrm{Siegel}})$$ be a Hodge embedding, with $G$ connected and similitude character $c$. For every prime $p$ there exist a totally real field $P$, a connected reductive group $J$, and a Hodge embedding $$(J,X_J)\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow
 (\mathop{\mathrm{GSp}}(W,\psi_W),X'_{\mathrm{Siegel}})$$ with the following properties.*

1.  *There are inclusions of Shimura data induced by $$G\longrightarrow J\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{Res}}_{P/\mathbb Q}G_P,$$ where the first map is diagonal and $J$ is the subgroup on which the similitude multipliers in the restriction of scalars agree.*

2.  *The group $J_{\mathbb Q_p}$ is quasi-split and has a full connected stabilizer $\mathcal J$ making $(J,X_J,\mathcal J)$ strongly admissible.*


3.  *As a rational $J$-representation, $$W\simeq (V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}P)^{\oplus m}
     \label{eq:transport-copies}$$ for some positive integer $m$. The form $\psi_W$ has multiplier the common character $c$, and $\mathcal J\to\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}(W_{\mathbb Q_p})$ extends to a closed immersion into $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}(\Lambda_p)$ for a self-dual $\mathbb Z_p$-lattice $\Lambda_p$.

Let $(J,X_J,\mathcal J)$ be strongly admissible, with $J_{\mathbb Q_p}$ quasi-split, and choose the adapted embedding and neat level above. Let $x\in\mathcal S_K(\mathbb F)$ have a lift to characteristic zero. Suppose a filtration $\mathcal F$ on $D_x$, after a finite extension of $K_0$, has the following properties:* 1. *the resulting filtered isocrystal is admissible;* 2. *geometrically its filtration is induced by a $J$-valued cocharacter in the conjugacy class prescribed by $X_J$.* *Then, after extending that field finitely, there are $y\in\mathcal I_x$, a tensor-preserving quasi-isogeny $b:C_x\to C_y$, and a lift $\widetilde y$ over the extended valuation ring such that $$b^*\mathop{\mathrm{Fil}}^1 H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(C_{\widetilde y})=\mathcal F^1$$ under the crystalline–de Rham identification.* *In particular, condition (1) follows if the filtered isocrystal and its tensor data have finite local-field descent and $\mathcal F$ is weakly admissible.

Let $A/\overline{\mathbb Q}$ be an abelian variety of positive dimension with good reduction at $w$, and let $\gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\mathbb C),\mathbb Q(r))$ be a rational Hodge class, where $0\leq r\leq\dim A$. There are a positive integer $n$, a CM abelian variety $B/\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction at $w$, a rational Hodge class $\kappa$ of codimension $r$ on $B$, and a quasi-isogeny $a:A_0^n\to B_0$ such that $$\gamma_0=(aj)^*\kappa_0,$$ where $j:A_0\to A_0^n$ is the first-factor inclusion. This is an equality of the usual absolute-Hodge specializations in every prime-to-$p$ realization and in crystalline cohomology extended to $C_w$.

Let $A_0/\overline{\mathbb F}_p$ be an abelian variety equipped with a rational action of a CM field $E$ and a polarization whose Rosati involution restricts to conjugation on $E$. Suppose that $$D=H^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\overline{\mathbb F}_p))[1/p]$$ has rank $2s$ over $E\otimes_\mathbb QK_0$, where $s\geq 1$. Suppose also that there is an invertible $u\in\mathop{\mathrm{End}}^0(A_0)$ such that $$u^\dagger=u,\qquad ue=\bar e u\quad(e\in E).$$ Let $\beta$ be the dual polarization pairing on $D$, with values in the isocrystal line of slope $1$.*

*Then there are a finite extension $K/K_0$ and a subspace $L\subset
D_K$ with the following properties:*

1.  *The one-step filtration with $\mathop{\mathrm{Fil}}^1D_K=L$ is weakly admissible.*

2.  *$L$ is stable under the cohomological actions of $E$ and $u$, and is Lagrangian for $\beta$.*

3.  *After extending to an algebraically closed field $\Omega/K$, one has $\dim_\Omega L_\tau=s$ for every embedding $\tau:E\hookrightarrow\Omega$.*

4.  *The isocrystal, its indicated tensors, and this filtration have finite local field descent.*

*Moreover, geometrically $L$ belongs to the balanced polarized cocharacter orbit. More explicitly, define $$G_D=\left\{g\in\mathop{\mathrm{GSp}}(D,\beta)\cap
 \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}_{E\otimes_\mathbb QK_0}(D):
 \det_{E\otimes_\mathbb QK_0}(g)=c(g)^s\right\},$$ where the scalar on the right is viewed in $(E\otimes_\mathbb QK_0)^\times$. The balanced $E$-stable $\beta$-Lagrangians form a single $G_D(\Omega)$-orbit. Each is the weight-$1$ space of a cocharacter of $G_{D,\Omega}$ with weights $0,1$. In particular $L$ belongs to the orbit of any original filtration of this type under a tensor-preserving comparison.

Let $K_1/K_0$ be a finite extension, and let $r,b\geq 1$ be integers. There exist an element $\theta$ algebraic over $\mathbb Q_p$ and a point $$(x_0,\ldots,x_{r-1})\in K_1(\theta)^r$$ at which every nonzero polynomial in $K_1[X_0,\ldots,X_{r-1}]$ of total degree at most $b$ is nonzero. The coordinates $x_i$ can all be chosen in $\mathbb Q_p(\theta)$.

Let $M$ be a symplectic space of dimension $2m$ over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $W\subset M$ have dimension $a$. A nonempty open subset of the Lagrangian Grassmannian consists of subspaces $L$ such that $$\dim(L\cap W)=\max(0,a-m).$$ On any fixed symplectic affine big cell, at least one nonzero polynomial of degree at most $m$ has nonvanishing locus contained in this open subset. This degree bound is independent of $W$.
The filtration of Theorem 10, with its finite local field descent, is admissible: the descended filtered isocrystal is the filtered crystalline module of a crystalline representation.

Let $D,L$ be as in Theorem 10, and let $\psi$ and $U$ denote the homological polarization and the homological action of $u$ on $D_K^\vee$. The untwisted divisor form $\psi(\cdot,U\cdot)$ belongs to $$\mathop{\mathrm{Fil}}^1\bigl(\bigwedge^2D_K\bigr)=L\wedge D_K,$$ and hence to filtration degree zero after its codimension-one Tate twist. If a marked power is realized by an abelian lift, the corresponding pulled-back divisor satisfies the filtration condition for its symmetric homomorphism in Lemma 5.

Every $\gamma\in W_E^s(A)$ satisfies the Lefschetz pairing property at $w$. More precisely, if $\mathcal U$ in [eq:weil-U] has no invertible element, all complementary pairings are zero. If it has an invertible element, $\gamma_0$ is a simultaneous rational Lefschetz class.
If $\mathcal U$ contains no invertible element, every specialization of a class in $W_E^s(A)$ is orthogonal to all complementary Lefschetz classes, in each cohomological realization.

Let $B$ be a complex abelian variety, let $R\in\mathop{\mathrm{End}}^0(B)$ be a rational projector, and suppose that there is an algebra action $E\longrightarrow R\mathop{\mathrm{End}}^0(B)R$ whose unit maps to $R$. Let $T=\operatorname{im}(R)$ in rational first homology, with $\dim_E T=2s$; the indicated endomorphisms act by zero on $\ker(R)$. Suppose there is a rational divisor class $D$ on $B$ such that $R^*D=D$ and, after splitting $E$, its alternating form is $$D=\sum_\tau D_\tau,
 \qquad D_\tau\in\bigwedge\nolimits^2 T_\tau^\vee\otimes\mathbb Q(1),$$ with each $D_\tau$ nondegenerate. Then the rational subspace whose scalar extension is $$\bigoplus_\tau\bigwedge\nolimits^{2s}T_\tau^\vee\otimes\mathbb Q(s),$$ extended by zero on the complementary summand, consists of rational Lefschetz classes on $B$.

The Hodge homomorphism of $A$ factors through $G$, and its conjugacy class defines a Shimura datum of Hodge type through the displayed embedding. Over an algebraically closed coefficient field, the orbit of the corresponding filtration on $H^1$ consists exactly of the $E$-stable Lagrangians for the dual polarization pairing whose dimension at each embedding of $E$ is $s$. Using a basis of its Tate line, every alternating form in [eq:weil-pure-space] transforms by $c^s$.

Let $A/\overline{\mathbb Q}$ be an abelian variety of CM type with good reduction at $w$, and let $r>0$. For every rational Hodge class $\gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\mathbb C),\mathbb Q(r))$, there are finitely many abelian varieties $B_i/\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction at $w$, rational homomorphisms $f_i\colon A\to B_i$, and rational Weil classes $\eta_i\in H^{2r}(B_i(\mathbb C),\mathbb Q(r))$ such that $$\label{eq:cm-pullback-decomposition} \gamma=\sum_i f_i^*\eta_i.$$ Each $B_i$ has an action of a CM field $K$ for which $H_1(B_i(\mathbb C),\mathbb Q)$ has rank $2r$ over $K$, the Hodge signatures are $(r,r)$ at every embedding of $K$, and a polarization induces complex conjugation on $K$. The equality specializes simultaneously in all the realizations used in Theorem 1.
The Lefschetz pairing property holds for the specialization of every rational Hodge class on a CM abelian variety over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction at $w$.

For every abelian variety $A/\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of dimension $d$ with good reduction $A_0/\mathbb F$ at $w$, every $0\leq r\leq d$, and every rational Hodge class $$\gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\mathbb C),\mathbb Q(r)),$$ there is a unique class $\rho_\gamma\in\mathcal R^r(A_0)$ such that $$(\rho_\gamma)_\ell=\gamma_{0,\ell}\quad(\ell\ne p),\qquad (\rho_\gamma)_p\otimes 1=\gamma_{0,p}.$$ The prime-to-$p$ equalities are in $H^{2r}_{\acute{e}t}(A_0,\mathbb Q_\ell(r))$; the crystalline equality is in $$H^{2r}_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\mathbb F))[1/p](r) \otimes_{K_0}C_w.$$ The specialization components are those of Theorem 1. The assertion holds for every prime $p$, including $p=2$, with the prime, place, and theory fixed before $A$ and $\gamma$ vary.

Fix the prime and place as in Theorem 1. Let $A/\overline{\mathbb Q}$ be an abelian variety of dimension $d$ with good reduction $A_0/\mathbb F$ at $w$, and let $\gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\mathbb C),\mathbb Q(r))$ be a rational Hodge class, where $0\leq r\leq d$. There is one rational algebraic cycle $z_\gamma\in\operatorname{CH}^r(A_0)_{\mathbb Q}$ such that $$\operatorname{cl}_\ell(z_\gamma)=\gamma_{0,\ell} \quad(\ell\ne p),\qquad \operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{cris}}(z_\gamma)\otimes1=\gamma_{0,p}.$$ The crystalline equality is in $$H^{2r}_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\mathbb F))[1/p](r) \otimes_{K_0}C_w.$$ This holds for every prime $p$, including $p=2$. Consequently, for every $y\in\operatorname{CH}^{d-r}(A_0)_{\mathbb Q}$, the traces of $\gamma_{0,\ell}\operatorname{cl}_\ell(y)$ for $\ell\ne p$ and of $\gamma_{0,p}\operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{cris}}(y)$ are all the same rational number $\deg(z_\gamma\cdot y)$.
